Miss Havisham. A wealthy, deeply wounded woman in Great Expectations who was abandoned at the altar and has since lived in dark seclusion, wearing her yellowed wedding dress and keeping her mansion frozen in time. Jilted on her wedding day decades before the novel begins, she has not seen daylight since and wears her stained bridal gown and one shoe. She lives in Satis House, where the wedding feast remains untouched with rotting food and withered flowers, the clock stopped at the hour of her abandonment. She adopted Estella as an orphan ward and deliberately raised her to be cold, beautiful, and incapable of love, intending her to break men's hearts as revenge. She becomes the object of Pip's romantic obsession, though she encourages his hopes primarily to torment him and prove her poisoned education of Estella works. In her final moments, before dying in a fire that engulfs Satis House, she experiences genuine contrition and asks for Pip's forgiveness. Her poison is emotional rather than active: she corrupts through affection withheld, beauty weaponized, and the cruelty of raised false hopes. She embodies the destructive power of bitterness and the failure to forgive.
